latin.565: §. XV. UNDECIMUM SECULUM Hildebrandinum vulgò dicitur, quod malitia & tyrannide Hildebrandi Papæ, seu Gregorii VII, omnium maximè infame est, cum Anti-Christianismus, i. e. Dominatus Tyrannisque Papalis, uti Seculo VII. in Bonifacio III, à Parricida Phoca, Episcopo Oecumenico constituto, plenam suam genituram consecutus, ita per artes Hildebrandinas Dictatusque hujus hominis insolentissimos, ad fastigium perductus est.
latin.566: Quemadmodum verò Tyrannis Hildebrandi in ipsos Imperatores, maxime in Henricum IV. sæviit, ita quoque veritatis Eucharisticæ Confessorem ejus Seculi Celeberrimum BERENGARIUM ANDEGAVENSEM, quanquam alia de causa, involvit.
latin.567: Equidem, quinam præcisè hujus præstantissimi Confessoris de Sacra Cœna loquendi modi fuerint, non adeò in proclivi est decernere, quod Scripta hujus Viri, ab inimicorum suorum numerosa turba, penitus oppressa deletaque sunt; Quid quòd, concedi potest, hunc ipsum Berengarium, Transsubstantiatorum, unô alioque jam tum seculo cristas erigentium, importunitate, eò zeli adactum fuisse, ut de S. Cœna commentatus, Figuræ crebrius Typique & Signi, quam Antitypi Corporisque Christi, in eadem, omnibus Fidelibus communicantibus præsentissimi, mentionem injecerit; interim fatendum insimul est, veritati, quà rem & substantiam, firmiter adhæsisse eum, etiamsi per inhumanitatem adversariorum suorum, aliquando passus aliquid humani videatur.
latin.568: Consensus ejus cum veritate partim ex Præceptoris ejus Fulberti, Carnotensis Episcopi, doctrina, partim ex Scriptis, Berengarii sententiæ oppositis hancque recensentibus, liquidò colligitur. Præceptoris doctrina ex Epistola ejus ad Adeodatum se clarè prodit, quando is inter cætera ita scribit: Mysterium fidei non visu corporeo, sed SPIRITU FIDEI in Eucharistia intuendum, quod enim substantia panis & vini apparet exterius, jam Corpus & Sanguis Christi fit interiùs; Non quod ore discernitur, sed quod affectu interiore degustatur. Exere igitur palatum fidei, dilata fauces spei, viscera charitatis extende & sume panem vitæ, interioris hominis alimentum. Iterum: De fide interioris hominis procedit divini gustus saporis, dum certè per salutaris Eucharistiæ infusionem influit Christus in viscera sumentis.
latin.569: Inter opposita verò Berengario Scripta, Lanfranci Cantuariensis de Veritate Corporis Domini in Eucharistia, liber eminet, sequentia Berengarii verba repetens: Per Consecrationem altaris, panis & vinum fiunt Sacramentum Religionis, non desinunt esse quod erant, sed ut in aliud mutentur & fiant quæ non erant. Iterum: Sacrificium Ecclesiæ duobus constat, visibili sacramento & invisibili re sacramenti, i. e. corpore Christi. Rursus: Sacramenta sunt Visibilia rerum divinarum signacula, sed res ipsæ invisibiles in eo honorantur.
latin.570: Etsi verò ex his similibusque verbis, perperam à nonnullis, Berengarius Consubstantiationis Fautor & Patronus conjecturari consuevit, tamen annumerandum hisce minimè esse vel ipse Rupertus Abbas Tuitiensis, Consubstantiationis Crassioris Auctor, primus & præcipuus, fateri ultrò nullus verebitur, quando Berengarium non tantum errantium Antesignanum facit, sed & errorem ejus in eo collocat, quod Sacramentum corporis & sanguinis Domini, nudum rei sacræ signum voluerit haberi. Ita enim Rupertus Consubstantiator, Veritatis Confessores oppugnat: Illi autem quid dicant, quid pro argumento afferant, inquit, non habent, nisi quod aliqui ex iis, dum volunt Sacramentum corporis & sanguinis Domini, solummodò signum esse sacræ rei, juxta errorem quondam Berengarii Turonensis … etiam B. Augustinum sentire ita putant (De Sacramento Eucharistico lib. 3. cap. 11. & 15.). Cetera de Berengario dicenda require suprà Annot. 3.

pass_a.565: §. XV. The ELEVENTH AGE is commonly called Hildebrandine, because by the malice and tyranny of Pope Hildebrand, or Gregory VII, it is most infamous of all, when Anti-Christianism — i.e. Papal Dominion and Tyranny — just as in the VIIth Age in Boniface III, constituted Oecumenical Bishop by the Parricide Phocas, it obtained its full birth, so through Hildebrandine arts and this man’s most insolent Dictates it was led to its summit.
pass_a.566: But just as Hildebrand’s Tyranny raged against the Emperors themselves, especially against Henry IV, so also it involved the most Celebrated Confessor of Eucharistic truth of that Age, BERENGAR OF TOURS, though for another cause.
pass_a.567: Indeed, what precisely this most excellent Confessor’s modes of speaking concerning the Sacred Supper were is not so easy to decide, because this Man’s Writings were utterly suppressed and deleted by the numerous crowd of his enemies; What is more, it can be granted that this very Berengar, by the importunity of Transubstantiators already in that age raising their crests, was driven by zeal to such a point that commenting on the Sacred Supper he more often injected mention of Figure and Type and Sign than of the Antitype and Body of Christ most present in the same to all communicating Faithful; meanwhile it must at the same time be confessed that he firmly adhered to the truth as to the thing and substance, even if through his adversaries’ inhumanity he sometimes seems to have suffered something human.
pass_a.568: His consensus with the truth is gathered clearly partly from the doctrine of his Teacher Fulbert, Bishop of Chartres, partly from Writings opposed to Berengar’s sentence and reviewing it. The Teacher’s doctrine shows itself clearly from his Epistle to Adeodatus, when among other things he writes thus: The mystery of faith is to be looked upon in the Eucharist not by bodily sight but by the SPIRIT OF FAITH; for what appears outwardly as the substance of bread and wine already becomes inwardly the Body and Blood of Christ; Not what is discerned by the mouth, but what is tasted by interior affection. Therefore exercise the palate of faith, dilate the jaws of hope, extend the bowels of charity and take the bread of life, the nourishment of the interior man. Again: From the faith of the interior man proceeds the savor of divine taste, while certainly through the infusion of the saving Eucharist Christ flows into the bowels of the one taking.
pass_a.569: But among Writings opposed to Berengar, Lanfranc of Canterbury’s book On the Truth of the Lord’s Body in the Eucharist stands out, repeating the following words of Berengar: Through the Consecration of the altar, bread and wine become a Sacrament of Religion; they do not cease to be what they were, but that they may be changed into another and become what they were not. Again: The Sacrifice of the Church consists of two things, the visible sacrament and the invisible thing of the sacrament, i.e. the body of Christ. Again: Sacraments are Visible seals of divine things, but the invisible things themselves are honored in it.
pass_a.570: Although indeed from these and similar words Berengar has customarily been wrongly conjectured by some as Favorer and Patron of Consubstantiation, yet that he is by no means to be numbered among these even Rupert Abbot of Deutz himself, first and chief Author of Crasser Consubstantiation, will freely confess, when he makes Berengar not only the standard-bearer of those erring but also locates his error in this — that he wished the Sacrament of the Lord’s body and blood to be held a bare sign of the sacred thing. For so Rupert the Consubstantiator attacks the Confessors of Truth: But what they say, what they bring forward as argument, he says, they do not have, except that some of them, while they wish the Sacrament of the Lord’s body and blood to be only a sign of the sacred thing, according to the former error of Berengar of Tours … even think Blessed Augustine feels so (On the Eucharistic Sacrament Book 3 ch. 11 and 15). The rest to be said concerning Berengar seek above in Annot. 3.

565: §.XV: the ELEVENTH age is commonly called Hildebrandine — most infamous by Pope Hildebrand (Gregory VII)’s malice and tyranny.
Papal dominion, born full under Boniface III (Phocas, Age VII), was driven to its summit by Hildebrandine arts and his insolent Dictates.
566: As Hildebrand’s tyranny raged against the Emperors — especially Henry IV — so it also involved that age’s most celebrated Eucharistic confessor.
BERENGAR OF TOURS — though for another cause.
567: His exact modes of speaking on the Sacred Supper are hard to pin down: enemies thoroughly suppressed and deleted his writings.

Under Transubstantiators’ pressure he more often stressed Figure, Type, and Sign than Antitype and Christ’s most-present Body — yet as to the thing and substance he firmly held the truth, even if adversaries’ cruelty sometimes made him look merely human.
568: Consensus with the truth is clear from his teacher Fulbert of Chartres and from writings that oppose and review his sentence.

Fulbert to Adeodatus: look on the Eucharist’s faith-mystery not with bodily sight but by the SPIRIT OF FAITH — outwardly bread and wine, inwardly Body and Blood; taste by interior affection; take the bread of life as the interior man’s food.
569: Among opposing books, Lanfranc of Canterbury On the Truth of the Lord’s Body stands out — and repeats Berengar’s own words.

By altar consecration bread and wine become a Sacrament of Religion yet do not cease what they were; the Church’s sacrifice is visible sacrament plus invisible res (Christ’s body); sacraments are visible seals — the invisible things are what is honored.
570: Some wrongly make Berengar a consubstantiation patron — even Rupert of Deutz (crasser consubstantiation’s chief author) refuses that and instead charges him with wanting a bare sign of the sacred thing.
Rupert attacks truth-confessors as having no argument but that bare-sign claim (ascribed also to Augustine). Rest on Berengar: see above, Annot. 3. Stop before §.XVI / next extract.

notes.570: Not consubstantiation; Rupert bare-sign charge; Annot.3.
